title: Retail Loan Book: Early Delinquency Review

findings.headline: Shared phone numbers go with very high delinquency
findings.detail: 9 phone values repeat across 42 loans. 83.3% of these reached 30+ days overdue at 6 months (about 35 loans), against 8.8% overall, and 81% missed their first payment against 2.3% overall. This pattern looks like possible fraud.

findings.headline: Delinquency has climbed since Q2 2025
findings.detail: The 30-days-overdue rate at 6 months rose from 6.6% in Q2 25 to 12.8% in Q1 26, almost double. Quarterly loan counts stayed near 1,000, so this is not a volume effect.

findings.headline: Personal and Card loans drive the deterioration
findings.detail: Personal loans went from 9.3% in Q1 25 to 21.0% in Q1 26, and Card from 11.2% to 20.2%. Car stayed near 6% (6.3% in Q1 26) and Home stayed at or below 1.1%.

findings.headline: Digital and self-employed loans show higher delinquency
findings.detail: Digital is at 13.0% against 5.8% for Branch, and self-employed is at 12.2% against 6.5% for salaried. Digital also has a lower average bureau score (715.4 against 733.7 for Branch). These groups overlap with product mix, so check them together.

findings.headline: Income is missing mainly for Partner loans
findings.detail: Income is missing for 6.9% of rows. 90.8% of the gaps are in the Partner channel, where 39.7% of loans have no income. Any income-based analysis will under-represent Partner loans.

next_steps: Review the 42 loans sharing phone numbers for application fraud and check the channel and source of each linked group.
Split the Q1 26 rise in Personal and Card delinquency by channel and employment to see whether Digital or self-employed lending explains it.
Ask the Partner channel owner why income is blank for 39.7% of loans and set a mandatory capture rule.

reviews.note: 42 rows, 83.3% is about 35 loans, 81% is about 34: numbers hold. Removed 'possible fraud' as a cause the data cannot show; severity kept.
6.6% to 12.8% is correct and 12.8/6.6 is about 1.9. Reworded the volume claim to the actual range of 984 to 1,038.
All rates match. Car ranged 4.7% to 6.3%, so 'near 6%' was loose. Replaced causal 'drive' with 'rises are concentrated in'.
Digital 13.0 vs Branch 5.8, self-employed 12.2 vs salaried 6.5, bureau 715.4 vs 733.7 all match the summary. Medium severity is fair.
6.9%, 90.8% and 39.7% match the summary. 39.7% of 793 is about 315, which is consistent with the 90.8% share of gaps.

conclusion: The draft is broadly sound after small wording fixes. The main concern is that delinquency has risen from 6.6% to 12.8% in three quarters, mostly in Personal and Card loans. First, split that rise by channel and employment, and review the 42 loans with shared phone numbers alongside it.
limits: This review uses summary figures only, so it cannot show causes, test whether product, channel and employment effects overlap, or confirm what the shared phone numbers mean.
